title: Fuselage — Cabin Floor — Replacement of the Seat Track Splice Straps by Corrosion-Resistant Items
abstract: Replacement of the mid cabin seat track splice straps by corrosion-resistant items installed wet, which moves the mid cabin floor corrosion inspection from the six-year to the twelve-year check.

sections.planning_reason: Twenty-two aircraft returning for their first six-year check showed pitting corrosion on the seat track splice straps in the bays next to the mid galley and the mid lavatory. Sixteen needed strap replacement and four needed a local seat track repair, which is a far more expensive event. All of the affected aircraft operate in tropical or coastal networks and the metallurgical report identified galley and lavatory spillage through the floor panel joints as the driver. Doing the change at the six-year check, when the floor is open anyway, avoids the seat track repairs entirely.
sections.description: The splice straps at each seat track joint between stations 41 and 48 are replaced by items in a corrosion-resistant alloy with a chromate-free primer, installed wet with sealant at every faying surface. The forward attachment lug is retained and re-shimmed to take up the thickness difference. Clevis pins and cushioned clamps in the same bays are renewed because they are disturbed by the work.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Remove the cabin seats and the floor panels between stations 41 and 48 in zones 241 and 251. Do the inspection task AMM-M-53-50-12-200-013-A on the exposed seat track and record any corrosion finding. Remove the existing splice straps and clean the faying surfaces to bare metal. Blend out corrosion inside the allowable limits and report anything outside them before continuing. Install the corrosion-resistant straps D5350129600648 wet with sealant, and re-shim the forward lug D5350115767196 to the measured gap. Install new clevis pins LN666073-13 and cushioned clamps EN220364-30 in the disturbed bays. Torque the joint and apply the sealant fillet to the standard practice. Install the floor panels and the seats, then do a seat track locking check and record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to all MERIDIAN models from MSN M00001 through M00341 that are still pre MOD-161330. Aircraft from the production cut-in onward already carry the corrosion-resistant standard. Freighter aircraft are covered for the forward cabin section only, because the main deck floor uses a different track family.
sections.material_note: Kit K5350-1041-01 contains the strap set for one aircraft, the pins, the clamps and the sealant. Lead time is twelve weeks. Removed straps are not returnable. Operators embodying at a six-year check are advised to order the shim set separately because the measured gap varies from aircraft to aircraft.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next scheduled six-year check, or within 72 months after the date of this Service Bulletin, whichever occurs first.
